note: Omits the clause 'all that you say I will do for you'.
Renders 'at once' as 'in it', adding 'in it' and omitting 'at once'.
Adds 'I do not seek anything' before 'except'; source has only 'except'.
Hebrew 'they commanded Joseph' rendered as 'they sent to Joseph'; the commanding idea is lost.
'Saying' is rendered as passive 'it was said to them,' changing the speaker.
The source's 'I also' is omitted; Arabic has only 'I have heard.'
Adds 'his people'; source says 'in his midst' (among him), not among the people.
Changes subject: source says the locust will not be able to see the land; Arabic says 'no one can see the land'.
Adds 'he showed his greatness' not in the source, which states only that they dealt arrogantly.
Adds 'unjustly' (ظلماً), a qualifier not in the source's absolute prohibition.
Hebrew has 'and he is found in his hand' (conjunction); Arabic renders it 'or is found', changing the condition to an alternative.
Adds that the owner accepts the oath; source says the owner shall take the animal, and adds 'the keeper' as subject.
Pronoun shift: 'its sound' (the robe's) instead of 'his voice' (Aaron's).
Adds clause 'and its blood is bound to its life' not in the source.
Hebrew 'with two' rendered as 'with one of the two,' changing the number/meaning
Renders 'and so forth' as 'and at that time', adding a temporal idea not in the source.
Statements turned into rhetorical questions ('Does the wise answer...? Does he fill...?')
Source question 'have you destroyed' rendered as a statement 'you have destroyed'.
Negation reversed: 'our substance is not cut down' becomes affirmative 'our resisters have perished'.
Arabic changes plural 'they clap their hands' to feminine singular 'she claps with her hands'.
Source says 'all his words'; Arabic says 'all his actions/deeds'.
Source 'they purify themselves' rendered as 'they retreat/withdraw', a different idea.
Source says 'his steadfast love'; Arabic says 'my mercy' (pronoun changed).
Omits 'Yahweh' in 'Lord Yahweh of hosts'.
Second-person 'you contended with her' changed to third person 'he contends'; 'he restrained/moaned' rendered 'he removed her'.
Source 'my mouth commanded' rendered as 'his mouth commanded' — person changed.
Omits 'from afar' (מרחוק); only 'from ancient times' is kept.
Arabic omits the predicate 'her cities have gone up'; it only names the cities.
Adds 'as it is written in it' twice and 'false' (كاذب) for the one who swears, not in source.
The hearing clause omits 'nations and languages'; only 'all peoples' hear the sound.
